title: Entitlement sampling, signal harvest, and SIEM adaptor specification
content:
Purpose
This doc proposes a lightweight, low-latency pipeline for harvesting permission-evaluation signals across Redwood services, a cohort-based sampling strategy to generate compact evidence artifacts for audits, and a specification for a SIEM adaptor to ingest those artifacts. Goal is to reduce noise, bound storage/cost, and preserve forensic capability during RBAC v2 rollout and post-rollout troubleshooting.

Background / motivation
- RBAC v2 introduces richer attribute checks and dynamic entitlements (time-bound, resource-anchored). Full-fidelity audit logs for every auth check will overwhelm downstream storage and SIEM ingestion (token volumes x requests).
- Current ad-hoc sampling has caused gaps in cross-service correlation and made evidence reconstruction expensive during incidents.
- We need a reproducible method to capture representative evidence for (a) periodic compliance proofs, (b) retrospective investigations, and (c) ML-driven anomaly detection on policy changes.

Design principles
- Deterministic cohorts: sampling should be reproducible given a request fingerprint and a stable cohort config (so reruns can produce same sample sets).
- Signal-rich artifacts: sampled items must contain enough context to answer compliance questions without storing raw payloads (policy version, attribute snapshot, decision trace, request meta, resource id fuzzy hash).
- Minimal PII: redact or hash user-identifying fields where not required by compliance. Separate pathway for privileged evidence retention under enterprise contracts.
- Backwards-compatible: non-sampled checks emit minimal counters to telemetry so SRE/metrics are unaffected.
- Pluggable SIEM adaptor: normalized JSON schema and batching semantics so downstream SIEMs (Splunk/Chronicle/Datadog-logs) can ingest efficiently.

High-level flow
1) Authorization decision executed in service (authN/authZ layer).
2) Every decision emits lightweight telemetry record (decision_id, outcome, policy_id, tenant_id, timestamp). These are low-cardinality and always sent.
3) Cohort sampler computes hash(decision_id, tenant_shard) and consults cohort config: sample or skip.
4) If sampled, service writes a detailed evidence artifact to an encrypted evidence store (S3-like) and pushes a compact pointer + metadata to the SIEM adaptor.
5) SIEM adaptor batches pointers and small artifacts and sends to configured SIEM with backpressure and retry.
6) Evidence retention, indexing and controlled access are managed by evidence-service.

Cohort-based sampling model
- Cohort keys: tenant_id (primary), operation_type (create/read/delete), resource_bucket (coarse resource class), and rollout_phase tag.
- Cohort algorithm: deterministic modulo-based sampling using SHA256(key || experiment_id) -> integer -> compare to per-cohort rate. This ensures reproducibility and even distribution across replicas.
- Sampling tiers:
  - audit-critical (100%): admin-level changes, cust-managed enterprise tenants flagged for full capture.
  - diagnostic (1-5%): random sample for production tenants used for policy/quality tooling.
  - policy-change window (100% for 48 hours): after policy updates we auto-raise samples for impacted cohorts.
  - on-error uplift: any denied request with side-effect or repeated retries triggers immediate sample.

Signal and evidence artifact schema (flat JSON fields only)
- artifact_id: UUID
- decision_id: UUID (trace id-friendly)
- timestamp: RFC3339
- service: service-name (e.g., serving-runtime)
- env: prod/stage/dev
- tenant_id: opaque-id (hashed if configured)
- resource_class: e.g., model, dataset, deployment
- resource_id_hash: sha256(resource_id)
- action: read/write/infer/rollout
- outcome: allow|deny|fallback
- policy_version: semver or hash
- decision_trace: pipe-delimited list of rule-ids (or a small decision DAG compressed)
- attributes_snapshot: compressed key=value list (only attributes relevant to decision: role, ip_region, time_of_day, k-anon tag)
- redaction_hint: list of fields removed and reason
- evidence_store_path: s3://... or prov-id
- retention_tier: short|standard|enterprise
Note: the canonical artifact stored in evidence-store can be larger (additional logs, request headers), but the SIEM payload should only contain the flat fields above plus a signed pointer. This keeps SIEM ingest sane.

SIEM adaptor spec
- Input: batch of compact artifacts (max batch size 200, max batch bytes 1MB).
- Output: one of the supported sinks (Splunk HEC, Chronicle Ingest API, Datadog Logs).
- Rate limiting/backpressure: adaptor must buffer with FIFO and expose metrics: queue_depth, write_rate, failure_rate. On sustained backfill the adaptor switches to pointer-only mode (no file contents) and emits an incident alert.
- Idempotency: adaptor should dedupe on artifact_id for 7 days.
- Security: all transmissions to SIEM must use mTLS and token rotation; payloads must obey tenant-level encryption flags.
- Mapping: provide transformation templates for each sink (e.g., Splunk: event=artifact_json, sourcetype=rbac_evidence, index=tenant-index). Keep mapping configs in git.

Evidence automation and QA hooks
- Post-sampling lint: evidence-service runs a lightweight validator on sampled artifacts to ensure schema, required fields present, and policy_version resolvable. Invalid artifacts are quarantined and routed to a QA queue.
- Evals integration: sampled artifacts are fed to the policy-evals pipeline to detect regressions in allow/deny rates for a given policy rollout.
- Alert rules: spike in denied-decisions sampling rate -> auto-raise pager; drift in attribute distributions -> Slack alert to policy owners.

Rollout plan (phased)
Phase 0 (pilot, 2 weeks):
- Enable deterministic cohort sampler in staging for serving-runtime and platform-api.
- Sample diagnostic tier at 5% for a few non-critical tenants.
- Validate artifact schema, adaptor connectivity to internal Splunk test index.
- Owners: Priya (lead), Diego (runtime).

Phase 1 (canary, 3 weeks):
- Expand to 10% for production read ops, enable policy-change window capture for config changes.
- Run SIEM adaptor in pointer-only dry-run mode (verify mapping).
- Run parallel reconciliation job to ensure sampled artifacts reference actual logs.

Phase 2 (gradual ramp, 6 weeks):
- Increase sampling across cohorts to target rates. Add enterprise tenants to audit-critical.
- Enable retention policies and evidence-service access controls.
- Run tabletop: reconstruct two historical incidents using sampled artifacts to validate coverage.

Phase 3 (stable):
- Default diagnostic rate to 1% and keep uplift rules. Document policies and hand off to SRE/security on-call.

Migration and compatibility notes
- Services without the sampler will continue to emit lightweight telemetry; we will roll adapters into them incrementally.
- Old audit exports (full logs) will be ingested into evidence-store for 90 days to allow correlation during transition.
- A small shim will allow conformance: if evidence-service cannot find artifact for pointer, it will call a backfill API tied to request traces.

SLOs & metrics
- Sampling determinism test: <0.1% variance across replicas for a given cohort over 24h.
- SIEM ingestion success rate: 99.5% 30-day moving average.
- Evidence retrieval latency (for archived artifacts): P90 < 10s for standard tier.

Operational runbook (quick)
- SIEM adaptor alert (queue_depth>50k): pause non-critical sampling, increase pointer-only mode, page adaptor owner.
- Schema validation failures > 1%: disable sampling for service and investigate schema change.
- Tenant access request for data: evidence-service generates signed temporary access and logs the access event.

Open questions / decisions to make
- Should resource_id hashing use salted tenant-specific salt or global salt? (tenant salt favors privacy; global salt helps cross-tenant correlation for infra audits).
- What is the canonical decision_trace compress format? protobuf vs compressed text?
- Retention tiers: what are default TTLs for short vs standard for compliance jurisdictions (EU vs US)?

Next steps
- Review with infra and legal: Tue 2026-03-02 (security review slot).
- Prototype adaptor for Splunk HEC by end of sprint (Q1).
- Create a lightweight test harness that can re-run cohort selection deterministically across past 30 days of telemetry.

Notes / scratch
- Slack threads: #rbac-v2-sampling, #siem-adaptors
- Related tickets: JIRA-SEC-4123 (cohort config service), JIRA-PLAT-998 (evidence-store encryption), JIRA-SRE-210 (adaptor resilience).
- Quick TODO: define per-tenant enterprise opt-in flow (self-serve toggle in console).

Unresolved: balancing forensic completeness vs SIEM cost; prefer conservative default (1%) and strong uplift rules.
